$about: Observations for the 2026-08-04 round. Backfilled from this session's direct extraction of cycles-lifecycle.md, timeline.md, refinement-bridge.md, full-loop.md, greenfield-core.md, node-stack.md, skills-write.md, skills-maintain.md, po-rescue.md, auto-trigger.md, add-anytime.md, and the FINDINGS-LEDGER.md triage of the 12 brownfield waves (bf-governance, bf-language, bf-lifecycle, bf-notcode, bf-platform, bf-thin, bf-monorepo, bf-ml, bf-critical, bf-review, bf-shapes, bf-closing) plus the wave-6 backfill and showcase-gap/promise-inventory. Every 'fix' link was checked against the real merged PR body text (`gh pr view <n> -R repository-standards/core|node --json body`) on 2026-08-04 - a case is marked fixed only when the PR body names that specific defect, not merely the same area of code. Cases with no fix link are open: logged, not built this round, exactly as the source reports and the ledger state them.

observations.evidence: Reproduced first-hand: the translator's `**` -> `.*` substitution does not consume the slash in front of it, so `**/payment/**` compiles to `^.*\/payment\/.*$`, which requires a directory before `payment/` and misses `payment/index.ts`. The same bug is duplicated in facts-check.mjs's own glob translator. Fixed: one shared implementation now (standard/scripts/lib/glob.mjs) replaces both drifted copies.

A Chinese spec with four unresolved items printed PASS; the heading check next to it fails closed on translation, so fixing that error by translating the heading text lands the author in the silent pass on the marker check. The standard tells adopters to write specs in their own language, so this is not a hypothetical - reproduced first-hand (bf-language F1).

Reproduced independently three times against the same underlying bug: refinement-bridge F2 built a 6-shape table (four shapes pass that should fail, including the shape the template's own required section invites); add-anytime F1 reproduced it by adding a fifth open question under a fresh heading; po-rescue F1 found the gate's own remediation advice ('record an explicit deferral under "## Clarifications"') cannot clear a marker at all, so following the gate's own advice literally does not fix the underlying gap it names. Fixed: check-spec-clarified.sh now also greps the bracket-marker family inside prose form, with a dedicated test suite the gate had none of before.

Reproduced twice, independently: cycles-lifecycle F2 wrote the manual's own example shape with a real one-place violation (SPEC-1 duplicated between a cycle and the pool) and got a clean 'OK - 9 intent(s) across 5 place(s), each in exactly one', reading zero rows from the added file; timeline F12 reproduced the identical zero-intents result from the same page. Fixed: docs/tree/docs-cycles.md's example is now the literal fixture cycle-guard-test.mjs runs against, so the page and the guard cannot disagree again.

refinement-bridge F1: no skill instructs writing any status transition besides the initial draft value, spec-reconcile never mentions status at all, and check-spec-clarified.sh - the only mechanical gate that exists - never reads the Status field at all. Reproduced: the clarify gate correctly FAILs when invoked directly on the doctored spec, while spec-structure, spec-guard --audit --block, cycle-guard.mjs and self-verify.mjs all stayed green regardless. Fixed: spec-structure now re-runs the real clarify gate against any spec claiming that status or live.

Confirmed independently three times: bf-lifecycle F1 (verified first-hand per the ledger), greenfield-core F9, and promise-inventory B3 all found SPEC.md:13 saying 'Rules are numbered R1-R24' while R25 is defined at SPEC.md:177 - and promise-inventory additionally found the anti-drift guard's own FACT_SURFACES list omits standard/SPEC.md, the one file that still carries the stale line. Fixed: the rule count is now a declared, checked fact.

Three independent confirmations: bf-governance F8, bf-lifecycle F10 and bf-language F5 (which additionally proved the mechanism with an English control) all reproduced the placeholder warning false-positiving on `<picture>`/`<code>` in foreign repos and going blind on non-ASCII placeholders; bf-language F4 reproduced the same locale-blindness class on spec-structure's persona check specifically. Fixed the same way as the clarify gate's translation fix.

Two independent reproductions of the same underlying gap, both explicitly noted as NOT covered by PR13's locale/placeholder fix (a different bug in the same script): skills-write F1 found the check is a three-way OR whose first arm (hasServes) passes any non-placeholder string without ever consulting docs/personas.md - three reproductions all exit 0, including a spec containing the phrase 'for whom' (a phrase idea-write itself instructs writing) and a spec with backticks stripped from both roster rows (emptying the parsed roster). greenfield-core F4 independently confirmed the roster-membership direction is unenforced, contradicting personas-write's own claim that a persona missing from the roster 'does not exist as far as R10 is concerned.' Not fixed this round - logged for a future pass.

observations.evidence: greenfield-core F10: --audit checks only that every spec has a map entry, never the reverse. Reproduced with three capabilities declared in the map and only one specced - the blocking full-tree audit reported 'OK (1 capability specs, all mapped)' while two capabilities have live code globs and no spec. This is now partially addressed by PR13's fourth audit check (a mapped capability with no spec) - see PR13's changelog entry.

Confirmed independently by three agents on the same underlying bug (the fsWalk fallback only fires when the tracked spec list is entirely empty, so any repo with even one already-tracked spec makes new untracked directories invisible): refinement-bridge F4, skills-write F5, and full-loop F4, plus showcase-gap noting the same class. Reproduced identically three times: before `git add`, `--audit` reports OK; after, it correctly fails naming the orphan. Not fixed this round.

observations.evidence: Confirmed independently by two agents: skills-maintain F4 found pre-pr-review's list includes `spec-guard.mjs --audit` and omits the diff-scoped `--base --block` CI actually blocks on - reproduced end to end, all local checks green, CI's real command exits 1. full-loop F5 found the mirror bug: pre-pr-review instructs the non-blocking `--audit` form specifically to 'avoid moving failures to CI', which is the one command form that cannot fail on the same orphan-spec defect (GATE-24). Together the two make the local pre-PR gate weaker than CI in two independent ways at once. Fixed: pre-pr-review now names both flags CI uses.

node-stack F2, reproduced three ways: (a) no exception - FAIL drift 1; (b) exception written into stack.manifest.json, the documented home - still FAIL drift 1, no note; (c) the identical exception written into standard.manifest.json instead - correctly excepted, drift 0. The escape hatch worked only in the 'wrong' layer, silently breaking the documented 'nothing is all-or-nothing' brownfield promise. Fixed: exceptions added to the array of keys merged from the stack manifest.

Confirmed fixed from the node side: ADAPTING.md now points at the real, working mechanism after the core-side fix landed; the node repo's own workaround (recording the exception in standard.manifest.json instead) is no longer needed.

node-stack F1, reproduced: self-verify's check for merge-class entries was pure file-existence, never content. Deleting the entire supply-chain policy block still reported drift 0/100%/compliant - even though the stack's own CI asserts these exact three keys on itself. Generalizes to all 8 merge-class stack entries. Fixed: a `requiredKeys` mechanism now lets a merge-class entry assert specific keys exist.

Verified end to end on the real starter after the fix shipped: the node stack switched to declaring the three keys directly on the manifest entry, deleted the now-redundant custom guard script that had been the workaround, and confirmed the substitution passes when the keys are present and fails by name individually when any one is stripped.

bf-critical F12: nvaccess/nvda ships README.md/SECURITY.md in lower case; self-verify's file check used existsSync, which is case-insensitive on macOS/Windows and case-sensitive on Linux CI - so the reported drift/adoption differed by platform for the identical repo state. Fixed: case-exact file existence, verified on the real bf-critical evidence (drift moved from a platform-dependent number to a single correct one).

Confirmed independently twice: bf-critical F1 (severe) reproduced drift 4-5 from the built-in skeleton where the real manifest gives 13-15, same command, same repo, same minute; bf-wave6-backfill F7 reproduced the identical class as a second confirmation. node-stack F4 additionally found the collapse total: deleting standard.manifest.json from a drift-0 tree silently drops all 8 stack files and the stack guard from the count too, with the one status line that would have signalled it living behind the same conditional. Fixed: the silent skeleton fallback now says so loudly instead of reporting a look-alike number.

Built and proved as part of the same content-verification pass that fixed GATE-27/29: excepting a failure moves one point from drift to excepted, never inflates the numerator (proved directly); a guard's own script cannot be excepted by presence (kind:"guard" removed rather than half-implemented, closing node-stack F9 and the parallel bf-notcode F9 finding that the same kind was documented in code comments and never implemented); the exception count is always printed, including zero; content exceptions may now scope to a subtree via a `/**` suffix, closing the wave-9 shapes finding that no per-locale waiver granularity existed (tldr-pages' real `--ignore TLDR003,TLDR004,TLDR015` shape).

This is the North Star metric's own load-bearing defect, confirmed independently three times on three different trees: skills-maintain F2 reproduced a 'sham update' (bump the pin and the manifest, change zero of 18 real file deltas) reporting drift 0/100%/compliant, and separately drift 0 with 19 of 20 skills present; the real showcase repo (showcase-gap) reported drift 0 - 100% adopted (49/49) while missing idea-write and carrying 12 drifted skills and 5 drifted guards; node-stack F1 (see GATE-27) found the merge-class analogue. Before/after proof on one fixture: old verifier reported 'drift 0 - 100% adopted (51/51)' with a deleted skill, a stale settings block and a changed .nvmrc; new verifier reports 'drift 3 - 96% adopted (67/70), 0 excepted', naming each one. Fixed: a hash lives in the manifest itself (regenerated by tools/manifest-hashes.mjs, checked by tree-check so it can never go stale in the producing repo); the manifest file itself is deliberately excluded from generic hashing, since it is the one file every adopter must edit (a near-miss caught before shipping - see wave-9 shapes F6).

Confirmed on three independent repos, the most severe instance zeroing out an entire required directory: bf-monorepo F1 found kibana's `.claude/skills -> ../.agents/skills` symlink (its own unrelated 31-skill system) pre-satisfies the manifest's altPath check, reporting drift 0/compliant on a repo with zero of the 20 lifecycle skills. bf-shapes F4 (svelte) and bf-thin F3/F12 (GacUI, openvino) reproduced the milder version - an unrelated skills directory or SECURITY.md satisfying the entry by coincidence rather than content. Logged with the wt-drift work as a gap, not built this round.

Reproduced: audit --block exits 1 naming the new spec directory. Fixed: spec-specify now registers a capability at mint time, and spec-reconcile reconciles the map before the PR.

observations.evidence: cycles-lifecycle F7: standard.manifest.json declares backlog.md as primary with docs/backlog.md as an altPath; cycle-guard.mjs and add-to-backlog handle both, but cycle-open/SKILL.md and cycle-close/SKILL.md name only docs/backlog.md - so a repo using the primary path (as core's own repo does) is instructed to cut rows from a file that does not exist there. The known fix for this exact bug class was applied to the guard and to one of three skills; the two cycle skills were missed. Fixed: cycle-open/cycle-close now resolve the backlog the same way the guard does.

Confirmed independently by two agents, and found live in the owner's own aligned fixture at baseline before any edit: timeline F1 and cycles-lifecycle F5 both found the guard scopes its scan to ## Intents only, never ## Outcome, so an intent recorded as returned but never actually landing there is invisible everywhere - not in the pool, not caught by the guard, not readable by timeline-update, falsifying tracking-work.md's own 'whatever did not finish returns to the pool' on the owner's own aligned fixture. Fixed: cycle-guard now checks the 'at least one' direction too.

cycles-lifecycle F11, reproduced two ways: pasting the same id into two teams' cycles with backticks passes clean; pasting it with a stale `blocked:` reference present gets diagnosed as 'the block no longer applies' - the wrong fix, since the id exists twice, not zero times. Related: F12 found adding a column at the front (rather than appending one) of the intents table also silently dropped rows from the count. Fixed: ids in backticks or bold, and column position instead of column name, are both now resolved correctly.

Confirmed independently by two agents on the same underlying bug: cycles-lifecycle F8 found the only four declared statuses (todo/doing/blocked/done) have no split slot, so the fixture invented a fifth ('split -> IMPL-3') outside the enum with nothing checking the vocabulary; timeline F3 reproduced the consequence directly - the staleness check tests status === "done" only, so a finished-but-split item is never recognized as done, and the guard actively certified a block on finished work as 'live' (1 live block(s), exit 0). Fixed: a `split:<id>` status value was added.

Fixed: resolved in ADR-029's favor - a cold start may produce a size-based shape, never a date.
